claims.text: Z.ai's release notes record GLM-4.5 on July 28 as a native agentic LLM, GLM-4.5V on August 11 as a vision reasoning model, and GLM-4.6 on September 30 as a coding-focused model with a 200K context window.
December entries add GLM-4.6V, AutoGLM-Phone-Multilingual for screen-driven mobile actions, and GLM-4.7 with coding/reasoning/agentic updates.

limitations: Performance superlatives in the release notes are vendor claims; use only release identity, dates, stated feature scope, and clearly attributed evaluation claims.
overrides.why_this_special: Adds a model family where coding, multimodal reasoning, and explicit mobile-action agents converge over the half-year.

claims.text: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas on October 21 as a browser with ChatGPT built in, with initial macOS availability.
OpenAI later described OWL as the architecture behind Atlas and published a December hardening update focused on prompt-injection attacks.

overrides.why_this_special: A single release arc connects an action-capable browser surface, its implementation architecture, and a concrete security-control problem within the same half-year.
overrides.grouping_note: Keep grouped as one Atlas story package, but retain launch, architecture publication, and security hardening as three separate dated events.

claims.text: OpenAI launched ChatGPT agent with research, browser automation, and code/tool execution capabilities under user guidance.
A system card published the same day documented the evaluated risk/control boundary for the agentic system.

overrides.why_this_special: Provides the early-H2 anchor for the shift from conversational assistance to user-visible action execution.
overrides.grouping_note: Announcement and system card are one release package with separate product and safety evidence.

claims.text: OpenAI released gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b as open-weight reasoning models under Apache 2.0 plus its usage policy.
The release positioned the models for reasoning/tool use and efficient local or self-hosted deployment; detailed performance remains vendor/model-card attributed.

limitations: Open weights do not imply an unrestricted data/training disclosure; openness should be described specifically in terms of weights/license and deployment.
overrides.why_this_special: Reintroduced OpenAI into open-weight deployment and immediately created a runtime-integration event across the ecosystem.
overrides.grouping_note: Release announcement and model card are one open-weight package.

claims.text: OpenAI announced GPT-5 and API availability on August 7, with developer controls and coding/tool-use positioning.
OpenAI published safe-completions as an output-centric safety-training approach associated with GPT-5 rather than relying only on hard refusals.

limitations: Benchmark and 'best' claims remain vendor-attributed; release, API availability, model identity, controls, and safety-method publication are primary facts.
overrides.why_this_special: The central August model release simultaneously changed the frontier model, developer surface, and safety-training story, making it a useful cross-layer anchor.
overrides.grouping_note: Treat consumer/model, API/developer, and safe-completions pages as one GPT-5 release package with separate events.

claims.text: OpenAI released Sora 2 with synchronized dialogue/sound effects and a new Sora app surface.
The same-day system card documents safety evaluation and mitigation for the video-and-audio model.

overrides.why_this_special: Represents native audio-video generation becoming a first-class model/product stack rather than a text-only frontier story.
overrides.grouping_note: Model announcement and system card are one multimodal release package.

claims.text: SGLang v0.5.1 included runtime/disaggregated-transfer and long-context/model-support work; v0.5.6 added support for DeepSeek V3.2/V3.2 Speciale, diffusion models, JIT kernels, and further model/runtime optimizations.

limitations: Release-note feature/performance statements are project claims; no independent benchmark reproduction is implied.
overrides.why_this_special: Shows serving infrastructure absorbing new model families and modalities within weeks or months of upstream releases.

claims.text: TensorRT-LLM 1.0 made its PyTorch-based architecture and LLM API stable/default and expanded model/LoRA/hardware support; v1.1 continued the late-period runtime line.

limitations: Feature and performance descriptions are NVIDIA project claims and are hardware/configuration dependent.
overrides.why_this_special: Provides vendor-optimized serving evidence that runtime APIs and architecture were stabilizing while model support churn continued.

claims.text: Transformers v4.54 highlighted kernels and Transformers Serve; v4.55 added immediate gpt-oss support; v4.57 added Qwen3-Next, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-OMNI MoE and other new model families.
The gpt-oss integration release occurred the same day as the upstream gpt-oss announcement, illustrating very short model-to-library uptake for a coordinated release.

limitations: Library support date is an integration event and must not be used as the upstream model's original release date.
overrides.why_this_special: Links upstream model churn to practical local/self-hosted integration and shows the library layer increasingly carrying serving/runtime concerns.

claims.text: vLLM v0.10 began V0 engine cleanup; v0.11 completed removal of V0 so V1 became the only engine and changed CUDA graph defaults; v0.13 continued model/tool-parser support and breaking configuration changes.

limitations: Project release notes establish software changes and dates; performance implications vary by workload and hardware.
overrides.why_this_special: Provides a longitudinal serving-runtime spine across the half-year, useful for separating model announcements from the infrastructure needed to operate them.
